Trend boxes are marked based on the previous 12 months. The first column represents a 6-month period while the second two columns represent 3 months each. It is more relevant indicator of the current market to consider several buying cycles. All listing status' are included in the data set this gives a better picture of the subject's overall market activity within the defined market area. Annual Average $p/sf is $280.43, while the $p/sf for 7-12 month period was $286.37, and the next 4-6 month period was $261.97, current 0-3 mon period is $300.74. Annual Median $p/sf is $288.49, while the $p/sf for the 7-12 month period was $289.66, and the next 4-6 month period was $271.16, current 0-3 month is $298.23. Recent increases in mortgage lending rates are a concern for the continued trends. It is very likely that values will be impacted as increasing mortgage rates reduce purchasing power.

VALUATION_METHODS._AdditionalDescription:
PROPERTY DATA COLLECTOR: Jesse Speth
USPS ADDRESS: The address reported on the appraisal form is according to US Postal Service records as required by UAD format. The title company reports the city or county address and the title report may or may not match to USPS records. Subject was ordered with the address as 147 W Main, Newton UT 84327.PLAT MAP DIMENSIONS: The Plat attached with this report was provided by Cache County, no other survey or land description beyond the legal description was provided nor available to the appraiser. The plat map dimensions show that the subject has 36300 sf. The county data states the subject has .83 Acres. The lot dimensions provided on the plat map are as accurate as provided by the county. Some dimensions may not have been provided on the subjects parcel and were obtained based on surrounding lots dimensions. Appraiser has chosen to rely upon the plat map dimensions.
FINISHED LIVING AREA: The finished living area (gross living area (GLA) and non-GLA area) has been calculated using the Square Footage-Method for Calculating based on the ANSI Z765-2021 Measuring Standard as per Fannie Mae scope of work.
HIGHEST AND BEST USE: The highest and best use of the property considers the maximum market value of the property as both vacant and as improved. The following four tests are applied to the property, and all must be met, both as vacant and improved. First, is the use legally permissible? Second, is the use physically possible? Third, is the use financially feasible? Finally, is the use maximally productive of the property? This area is currently slowly transitioning from agricultural to residential. The highest and best use of the subject is its current use of a single family residence with agricultural rights. There was no commercial farming activity present at the time of inspection. While zoning allows for a smaller .5 acre lot the subject does not have enough frontage for more than the existing lot. The subject larger lot is considered surplus. Excess Land and Surplus Land: Excess land is often confused with surplus land. It is too often lumped in with the value of the entire property or ignored altogether. Excess land may be sold off separately from the rest of the property, so in effect, the subject property becomes two subject properties. Excess land may have a different highest and best use than the rest of the site. This must be addressed in the highest and best use analysis. Further, excess land will have to be treated separately in the valuation process. An entirely different set of comparable data may be required. The value of excess land must be reported separately. Surplus land does not have a separate value, as it cannot be sold off separately. It is “extra” land that may or may not contribute value to the overall property. It does not have an independent highest and best use. It may have the same value per unit of comparison (e.g., value per square foot, value per acre) as the rest of the site, or it may contribute less per unit of comparison. Source is Appraisal Institute common errors and issues January 1, 2013.

SALES_COMPARISON._Comment: The comparable sales selected are the most similar disclosed sales. Adjustments reflect the different features as valued by the market and not the cost of the amenity. Typically these differences included: size, parking, baths, fireplaces, out buildings, etc.Differences in GLA were adjusted $48p/sf, which was derived as follows: Replacement cost new (Marshal&Swift/Local builder) less physical depreciation (ref to cost apprch) less market difference of 55% ($160.65-33%=$107.11-55%=$48.20 ($48r) basement shell at $20p/sf and finish by room count for utility rather than percent of finish. The number of rooms contribute more to value than does the percentage of finish and real estate agents tend to more accurately report the number of finished rooms than correctly estimating the percent of finish. Some Net and Gross adjustments are higher than ideal due to Lot size and basement finish differences and lack similar disclosed sales. Adjusted value range from sales comparison approach is $354,000 to $391,000(r) See additional comps and comments on next page.
